text:
Maria: quick sync — can we route certain low-tier traffic to cheaper model variants automatically when it won't harm UX?

Aj: finance did a quick calc. big upside if we divert some percent to a quantized small model. need safe defaults.

Sahil: important: define measurable guardrails. for chat routes we must keep hallucination/safety within limits. no silent regressions.

Lisa: UX: console should let customers opt-in/out and show expected savings + estimated quality delta. also expose a per-route "fallback cap".

Kevin: sample routing policy shape I'm experimenting with:
```
policy = {
  "selector": "low_tier",
  "fallbacks": ["rwd-small-q8","rwd-small-q6"],
  "max_fallback_pct": "30%",
  "min_quality_score": 0.93
}
```
not final but workable.

Maria: good start. prefer making fallback visible in billing/latency dashboards so customers understand what's happening.

Aj: telemetry checklist: tag each request with routing_decision, primary_model, chosen_variant, fallback_reason, and attach a short sample response id for offline review.

infra-bot: routing-proto v0.3 scheduled to canary in us-east-1 in 20m. monitor: https://console.redwood/infradash/deploys/1762345678

Sahil: realtime quality score is tough. propose heuristic proxy (perplexity-ish metric + light safety heur) for immediate decisions, and weekly calibration jobs with more expensive evals.

Lisa: also add a per-customer cap toggle in console: a slider to limit fraction of traffic eligible for fallback. default conservative for new customers.

Kevin: billing tie-in: if fallback reduces token consumption, credit the customer-level cost dashboard and record estimated $ saved in the usage record.

Maria: governance: low-tier default = fallback ON with strict thresholds; mid/enterprise = OFF by default and requires explicit approval. document in onboarding.

Aj: alerting: fire if fallback_rate > 50% or quality_score_drop > 5% for > 10m. page only for enterprise SLOs, otherwise post to channel.

Sahil: samples retention: for privacy we should redact PII and only keep short snippets. low-tier samples 24h retention; enterprise configurable. need compliance review.

Lisa: I'll prototype the policy editor mockup — will include an "experiment mode" checkbox for canarying fallback percentages.

Kevin: implementation question: MVP single-step fallback (primary -> variant). cascading fallbacks add routing complexity; maybe v2.

Maria: agreed MVP = single-step. measure, then iterate.

Aj: bench numbers: routing 40% low-tier to q6 gives ~20% token cost reduction in our runs. sharing details with finance channel.

Maria: action items:
- Aj: finalize benchmarks and back-of-envelope cost model (due Friday EOD)
- Sahil: telemetry schema + PII redaction plan (due Tue)
- Lisa: console mockups + experiment UX (alpha next week)
- Kevin: implement policy protobuf + unit tests (PR this sprint)

Kevin: one more thing — should routing decisions be sticky per session to avoid jitter? I vote yes for chat sessions.

Sahil: sticky by conversation ID sounds right. saves user confusion. record sticky_assignment in telemetry.

Maria: good call. stickiness + percentage cap for experiment mode. reconvene after canary metrics are in. thanks all :tada:

deploy-bot: canary deployment started for routing-proto v0.3 in us-east-1 — watch: https://console.redwood/infradash/deploys/1762345678

Lisa: posting mockups in #design shortly.

Aj: shared bench outputs in #finance.

Maria: closing thread, follow-ups in next sprint planning. ping me for blockers.
